statement: The core asserts pcpi_valid, outputs the instruction word on pcpi_insn, and outputs the rs1 and rs2 register values on pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2.

not_verified.note: This binds the master (PicoRV32 core). The DUT is the PCPI slave. It is used as a stimulus constraint in CHK-004..CHK-009: pcpi_valid is asserted with pcpi_insn/pcpi_rs1/pcpi_rs2 and held stable until pcpi_ready.

statement: An external PCPI core can decode and execute the instruction and assert pcpi_ready when execution is finished.
The PCPI core can optionally write a result value to pcpi_rd and assert pcpi_wr.
The PicoRV32 core decodes the rd field of the instruction and writes the pcpi_rd value to the respective register.

not_verified.note: The register-file write-back is done by the core, not the DUT. The DUT side (pcpi_rd value when pcpi_wr=1) is checked in CHK-004..CHK-007.

statement: An illegal instruction exception is raised and the respective interrupt handler is called.

not_verified.note: Raising the illegal-instruction exception is core behaviour. Its 16-cycle bound is used as the acknowledge deadline the DUT must meet in CHK-008(a).

statement: The PCPI core should assert pcpi_wait as soon as the instruction is decoded successfully and keep it asserted until it asserts pcpi_ready.
Asserting pcpi_wait prevents the PicoRV32 core from raising an illegal instruction exception.

not_verified.note: How the core reacts to pcpi_wait is master behaviour. The DUT's pcpi_wait timing is covered by CHK-001 and CHK-008.

statement: mul multiplies rs1 by rs2 as XLEN-bit values and writes the lower XLEN bits of the product to the destination register.

not_verified.note: MUL is not implemented by picorv32_pcpi_div (a division/remainder coprocessor).

statement: mulh, mulhu and mulhsu return the upper XLEN bits of the 2×XLEN-bit product for signed×signed, unsigned×unsigned and signed rs1×unsigned rs2 respectively.

not_verified.note: MULH/MULHU/MULHSU are not implemented by picorv32_pcpi_div.

statement: Use mulh (or mulhu/mulhsu if appropriate) rdh,rs1,rs2 followed by mul rdl,rs1,rs2 to obtain both halves.

not_verified.note: This is a recommended software code sequence. There is nothing to observe at the DUT.

statement: Source specifiers rs1 and rs2 must be in the same order in both instructions, and rdh must not be the same as rs1 or rs2.

not_verified.note: This is a register-allocation constraint on software. Multiply is also not implemented by this DUT.

statement: Microarchitectures may fuse the two instructions into a single multiply operation instead of two separate multiplies.

not_verified.note: This is an optional microarchitectural fusion of multiply, which this divider DUT does not implement.

statement: mulw multiplies the lower 32 bits of the source registers and writes the sign extension of the lower 32 bits of the result to the destination register.

not_verified.note: MULW is RV64-only. The DUT is XLEN=32 (pcpi_rd is 32 bits).

statement: Signed arguments must be proper 32-bit signed values and unsigned arguments must have their upper 32 bits clear.

not_verified.note: This is an RV64 software usage note for MUL. It does not apply to a 32-bit divider.

statement: div and divu perform XLEN-bit signed and unsigned division of rs1 by rs2 rounding towards zero; rem and remu return the remainder of the corresponding division.
The sign of a nonzero rem result equals the sign of the dividend.
Use div rdq,rs1,rs2 followed by rem rdr,rs1,rs2 (or divu and remu if appropriate).

not_verified.note: This is a recommended software code sequence. Each DIV/REM is still checked on its own in CHK-004/CHK-005.

statement: rdq must not be the same register as rs1 or rs2.

not_verified.note: This is a software register-allocation constraint. The DUT does not write registers, and the rd field is ignored at the PCPI interface.

statement: Microarchitectures may fuse the two instructions into a single divide operation instead of two separate divides.

not_verified.note: Optional fusion (MAY) of div+rem is an internal microarchitectural choice. Results are still checked per instruction in CHK-005.

statement: divw and divuw divide the lower 32 bits of rs1 by those of rs2 as signed and unsigned and write the 32-bit quotient sign-extended to 64 bits in rd; remw and remuw give the corresponding remainders.

not_verified.note: DIVW/DIVUW/REMW/REMUW are RV64-only. The DUT is XLEN=32.

statement: remw and remuw always sign-extend the 32-bit result to 64 bits, including on a divide by zero.

not_verified.note: REMW/REMUW sign extension is RV64-only. The DUT is XLEN=32.

statement: Division by zero returns all bits set (-1 for div/divw, 2^L-1 for divu/divuw) as quotient, and the remainder equals the dividend for rem/remw/remu/remuw.
On signed overflow the quotient equals the dividend (-2^(L-1)) and the remainder is zero.
